title: Marisol in the Lot
hook: A bike is closing on your left toward the same exit.
scene: Rain hammers the old Kent Station lot, a sheet off the mesh, the stalls faded to ghosts. You are rolling a lane of painted arrows toward the exit onto 1st. In the left side mirror, a bicycle: bare head, dark jacket, fast, unafraid. Marisol. She is using the lot as a cut-through the way she always has. She is on your left rear quarter — the driver's side — closing to pass you on the inside toward the same exit. Your window is up. Your door is a weapon if you forget she is there.
decision: Marisol is in your left mirror, coming up the driver's side toward the same exit. What do you do?

options.text: Hold your line and let her find a way around — the lot is yours
options.result: You occupy the arrow. She has to squeeze between your door and a cart corral. Her bar-end kisses the steel plating with a sound like a dropped wrench. She stays up. She also puts a hand out, not a wave. You taught a courier that cars do not look.

options.text: Slow, stay right of the arrows, and give her the whole left side through the exit
options.result: You lift and drift right inside the stall paint. She takes the left at speed, three clear feet of wet asphalt, and is through the exit before you. Two fingers off the bars without looking back. The rain covers the rest. You roll out after her at a walking pace.

options.text: Tap the horn so she knows you see her
options.result: The horn cracks off the storefront and the parking deck. Marisol flinches and the front wheel tucks. She saves it. Every Quiet thing using this lot as a sit has your range now. She looks at you once, jaw set, and takes the exit anyway.

options.text: Speed up to beat her to the exit and clear the conflict
options.result: You get there first by a car length. She is still on your left rear when you start the turn onto 1st. Your rear quarter walks through the space her front wheel needs. She bails onto the sidewalk and the bike hits a cart corral. Steel, loud, done.

debrief: Give bicyclists at least three feet when you share a space, more in rain. Check the left mirror, then give her the whole left side. A horn cost you the quiet lot.

source.teaching_target: Pass bicyclists with at least three feet of space; check the left mirror before occupying a shared exit on the driver's side.

image_brief.subject: a woman on a bicycle riding PARALLEL to a faded matte-pink Baja VW Beetle, same direction of travel, at the car's LEFT rear quarter — the left flank of the car, the left door with riveted steel plating. She is slightly behind the door, closing to pass. Bare head, wet dark hair, dark jacket, no helmet, no delivery backpack. The bike is not aimed at the car. Both are heading toward the lot exit.
image_brief.foreground: wet faded stall paint and a rust-streaked cart corral on the far side of the aisle
image_brief.midground: her front wheel in the narrow wet gap beside the LEFT door; three feet that do not yet exist; she and the car share one heading
image_brief.background: heavy rain, Kent Station lot, gray storefront, dusk
image_brief.read: she is riding parallel in the left door zone of a moving car, same direction, and the exit is one lane wide
